title: Tournament routines
summary: Before, during and after the game: preparation, warm-up, in-game habits, recovery, sleep and food.

steps.md:
A routine turns good habits into automatic ones, so your energy goes into the game:

- **Before:** sleep, light meal, hydration; a fresh look at your openings and an easy tactical warm-up (not hard calculation). Know the event rules: default time, draw-offer restrictions, devices.
- **During:** a fixed thinking routine (blunder check before every move), posture and breathing, time checkpoints (e.g. move 15/30), water and a small snack in long games.
- **After:** a short analysis (write down your thoughts), then rest. Full analysis later, with the error log.

steps.question: The tournament regulations do not mention default time. You arrive 5 minutes late. What happens under the FIDE Laws?
choices: You lose: if not specified, the default time is zero (Art. 6.7.1)
Your clock is started and you may play
steps.explain: Without a specific rule the default time is zero. Always arrive early and check the regulations.

steps.question: What is a sensible warm-up an hour before a round?
choices: A few easy puzzles and a quick review of your opening files
Two hours of hard calculation exercises
steps.explain: Easy tactics activate pattern recognition without draining energy; hard calculation and blitz tire you or tilt you before the game.

steps.question: Your phone is in your pocket during a game. Under most FIDE event rules this...
choices: May be forbidden: Art. 11.3 bans electronic devices in the playing area unless the regulations allow them, and a violation can lose the game
Is always allowed if it is switched off
Is only a problem if it rings
steps.explain: Know the devices policy of the event. Leave the phone in the bag or at the arbiter's table if required.

steps.question: After a hard loss late in the evening, with another round tomorrow morning, which plan is best?
choices: A short note of the critical moments, then food, rest and sleep; full analysis after the event
Analyse with the engine until 2 a.m.
steps.explain: Sleep and recovery protect the next game; deep analysis can wait. (KB sleep-and-stamina notes.)

steps.md: **Retrieval check.** Write your personal three-part routine (before / during / after) in five lines, and keep it in your scorebook cover.

sources: FIDE Laws of Chess (2023), Art. 6.7 (default time), Art. 11.3 (devices)
